title: Implement append-only manual-scan feedback
evidence_required: FT-002-AC-003 — RED: an accepted manual scan currently issues editMessageText for the busy state and again on completion, and successful scans with sent ads can omit an explicit completion message. GREEN: the accepted trace sends a fresh start message and later a distinct success-with-sent, zero-result, paused, or error completion message with zero edits; duplicate and active-backoff requests retain their existing rejection, capacity-one state, and busy-state release. Decisive comparison: captured Telegram methods change from busy/restore edits and conditional completion to start/completion sendMessage calls only, while request count, duplicate/backoff rejection, pause outcome, sent count, error outcome, and final busy state remain claim-equivalent. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-003-T2-FT-002-W1/TASK-003-T2-FT-002-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.
purpose: Make accepted manual scans visibly append-only through separate start and completion/error messages without moving or weakening Polling Application scheduler behavior.
success_outcome: Every accepted manual scan sends a fresh start message and a later fresh completion/error message with zero edits, while duplicate requests, active backoff, pause handling, capacity-one single-flight, and busy-state release remain unchanged.
anti_goals: Do not implement callback navigation/mutation, authorization-boundary rejection, text-input, or FT-002-AC-004 proof owned by TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1.
Do not change administrator authorization policy, pending-input behavior, Telegram offset durability, or shared settings ownership.
Do not move manual-scan queueing, capacity, pause, backoff, polling, or state transitions into Telegram.
Do not change internal/app production code, persistence, schema, configuration, dependencies, polling candidates, deployment, FT-001, or FT-003.
Do not remove or redesign the generic Telegram client edit API; only the owned manual-scan runtime flow stops calling it.

forbidden_scope: callback navigation/mutation, authorization-boundary rejection, and text-input behavior owned by TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1
internal/app production polling, scheduling, backoff, and state-transition behavior
internal/store schema, paths, or stored-row interpretation
administrator allowlist and target-chat authorization policy
stop_conditions: The manual-scan outcome requires a production change outside Telegram Adapter or a change to the existing Polling Application interaction contract.

Execution requires changing callback navigation/mutation, authorization policy, pending input, scheduler ownership, Polling Application production behavior, Telegram offset durability, SQLite, configuration, dependency graph, or production runtime.
Execution requires a project path outside the hard write boundary, excluding workflow-owned evidence and lifecycle bookkeeping.
Execution reveals an unresolved product behavior, public contract, data authority, tier, dependency, or task-boundary decision.
Execution cannot reproduce accepted start/completion/error and scheduler-state outcomes safely in the local httptest/app unit harness.
Execution cannot obtain honest RED/GREEN evidence for FT-002-AC-003.

constraints: Keep one Go modular monolith and the accepted package dependency graph.
Send accepted manual-scan start and completion/error feedback as separate fresh messages and make no manual-flow edit request.
Keep request capacity, single-flight, pause, backoff, polling, completion callback, and busy-state release in Polling Application.
Use app production behavior only as an unchanged provider through the accepted Telegram/Polling Application contract.
Use only the local Telegram httptest/in-memory Backend and app unit harness; no live Telegram, Somon, SQLite, or production probe is authorized.
The non-empty write boundary is hard and excludes internal/app production code.
invariants: An accepted manual scan emits fresh start and completion/error messages and makes no runtime editMessageText request.
Polling Application retains capacity-one manual-scan single-flight, pause, backoff, completion, and busy-state ownership.
Duplicate and active-backoff requests remain rejected without an additional queued poll.
Callback authorization, text-input state, persisted settings, Telegram offset, and SQLite behavior remain unchanged.
No client detection, edit retry/cache, deletion, persistence, schema, configuration, dependency, worker, compatibility layer, or duplicate scheduler owner is added.
verification_targets: FT-002-AC-003: captured accepted start and success-with-sent/zero-result/paused/error completion traces prove separate sendMessage feedback and zero edits, while app/backend state proves one queued request, duplicate/backoff rejection, unchanged pause behavior, completion values, and busy-state release.
Isolation and rerun: all Telegram calls target a local httptest server, Backend state is disposable, app scheduler proof is in-process, and no external request or durable state mutation occurs.
